{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "Tunisia Youth Impact uses cooking contests to encourage young Tunisian women in rural villages to vote in the presidential election."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "On Saturday, October 12, in the rural town of Echamine, the country prepares for the second round of the presidential election between Nabil Karoui and Kais Saied."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "The national turnout in the first round was just 48.98%."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "Tunisia Youth Impact holds Voticook cooking contests where participants vote for the winner to raise awareness about the democratic process."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "Wafa Tarhouni, president of the association, explains that the contest is a practice vote where women compete through their dishes to be elected by diners."}, {"id": "5", "subevent": "Volunteers replicate real voting conditions, including electoral lists, voting booths, and sealed ballot boxes, but replace the ink with a water and shampoo mixture."}, {"id": "6", "subevent": "In Echamine, the contest is held in the courtyard of Hinda Jlass's half-built home, where she prepares couscous."}, {"id": "7", "subevent": "Hinda Jlass says the event is a way to get together with other women and that participating is essential."}, {"id": "8", "subevent": "Hinda Jlass plans to vote on Sunday, which will be only the second time in her life."}, {"id": "9", "subevent": "At noon, seven competitors from the village present their dishes to around fifty electors."}, {"id": "10", "subevent": "The electors taste the dishes and vote using the same procedure as in the presidential election, with volunteers guiding them."}, {"id": "11", "subevent": "Members of the ISIE and EU observer Stefan Ziegler attend, with Ziegler saying it's original and good for Tunisian democracy."}, {"id": "12", "subevent": "After the vote, ballots are counted and volunteers point out mistakes that could invalidate a vote."}, {"id": "13", "subevent": "Najwa Jlass, the hostess's sister, wins the contest and says she will vote 'for real' the next day."}]}

{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "Crime adapts to societal changes, evolving from individual violations to more sophisticated organized structures."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "Present-day organized crime differs from the past, with the Sicilian Cosa Nostra adapting to economic changes from agrarian to urban-industrial."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "Organized crime has become networks and alliances across national boundaries, linking underworld with legitimate institutions."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "Narcotics trafficking leads to corruption, threats, and killings of law enforcement, and forces drug users to commit crimes."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "Drug proceeds are laundered and reinvested into the legal economy, intertwining common, economic, and organized crimes."}, {"id": "5", "subevent": "Organized crime seeks power monopoly and uses any means for profit, disregarding public interest and rules."}, {"id": "6", "subevent": "Common criminality and organized crime intersect, with many organized criminals starting as thieves, but organized crime involves continuity, hierarchy, and complex operations."}, {"id": "7", "subevent": "Organized crime develops a mythology and reputation of invincibility, which affiliates use to intimidate and threaten."}, {"id": "8", "subevent": "The reputation affects how mafiosi see themselves and are seen, with 'made members' viewed as glamorous and dangerous figures."}, {"id": "9", "subevent": "The complexity of organized crime makes it difficult to define, but informants' confessions have provided documentation."}, {"id": "10", "subevent": "Nigerian criminal groups are pervasive globally, with structures including pyramidal hierarchies, clan networks, and independent cells."}, {"id": "11", "subevent": "Nigerian criminals target the U.S. and Britain, with scams and frauds causing significant losses, such as the '419 scam' and check theft."}]}

{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "Marines downed a hostile Iranian drone on Thursday using a new electronic warfare system on the deck of USS Boxer."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "The drone was downed 1,000 yards from the amphibious warship during a transit through the Strait of Hormuz into the Persian Gulf."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "The Marine Air Defense Integrated System (MADIS) used electronic jammers, radars, and gun systems to take out the UAV."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "The version of MADIS aboard Boxer was mounted on an MRZR on the bow of the ship and powered by a gasoline electrical generator."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "The Marine Corps did not immediately respond to a request for additional information on the system."}, {"id": "5", "subevent": "Naval analyst and retired Navy officer Thomas Callender told USNI News that the encounter is the first known kill by a new generation of electronic warfare and directed energy weapons."}, {"id": "6", "subevent": "The Navy and Marines have been concerned about swarms of cheap but lethal unmanned vehicles that could overwhelm defenses."}, {"id": "7", "subevent": "The Navy has tested less expensive options at sea to shoot down drones, including 5-inch deck guns and the Phalanx Close-in Weapons Systems, with limited success."}, {"id": "8", "subevent": "In 2014, the Navy deployed a 30-kilowatt laser aboard a ship in the Persian Gulf as an early test of a directed energy weapon at sea."}, {"id": "9", "subevent": "The Navy is moving to install its first 60-kilowatt Lockheed Martin-built HELIOS directed energy weapon on a destroyer in 2021."}, {"id": "10", "subevent": "In January, Northrop Grumman won a contract to develop the SEWIP Block III electronic attack capability for U.S. warships."}, {"id": "11", "subevent": "Callender said using systems like MADIS is less escalatory than shooting a missile and could provide deniability in some scenarios."}]}

{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "An ancient gold coin described as a 'naked and shameless celebration' of the assassination of Julius Caesar set a new record for a coin sold at auction."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "The coin was bought by an anonymous bidder for £2.7 million ($3.5 million)."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "The coin features a portrait of Marcus Junius Brutus, one of the ringleaders in the assassination of Caesar in 44 BC."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "The coin also depicts the daggers used by Brutus and his co-conspirator Cassius to slay Caesar in the Theater of Pompey in Rome, and a cap of Liberty."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "The coin is inscribed with the phrase 'Eid Mar' (the Ides of March), referencing March 15, the date of Caesar's death."}, {"id": "5", "subevent": "The coin was issued by Brutus two years after the assassination, in 42 BC."}, {"id": "6", "subevent": "Richard Beale, managing director of Roma Numismatics, described the coin as a 'naked and shameless celebration' of the assassination in a press release."}, {"id": "7", "subevent": "Caesar's death was fueled by the belief among Roman politicians that he intended to make himself king."}, {"id": "8", "subevent": "Caesar was killed by a group of senators, including friends and people whom he had previously pardoned."}, {"id": "9", "subevent": "Brutus subsequently killed himself after losing the Battle of Philippi to Caesar's nephew and heir, Octavius, and friend Mark Antony."}, {"id": "10", "subevent": "The coin is in near-mint condition and is one of only three known to exist."}, {"id": "11", "subevent": "The previous record price for a Roman coin was set in 2008, when a bronze sestertius of the Emperor Hadrian sold for around $2.5 million."}, {"id": "12", "subevent": "The previous record for any coin was held by an ancient Greek gold stater, which sold for $3.25 million in 2012."}]}

{"subevents": [{"id": "0", "subevent": "Mars will be at its biggest and brightest in the night sky as it aligns with Earth."}, {"id": "1", "subevent": "The event, known as 'opposition', occurs when Mars and the sun are on directly opposite sides of Earth."}, {"id": "2", "subevent": "All three bodies will be in a straight line at roughly 11.30pm."}, {"id": "3", "subevent": "Mars will be at its best around 1am on Wednesday, according to the Royal Observatory Greenwich."}, {"id": "4", "subevent": "Hannah Banyard, an astronomer at the Royal Observatory Greenwich, said it's a really good chance to view it, noting the last time this happened was in 2018 but it was difficult to see because it was low on the horizon."}, {"id": "5", "subevent": "She added that for about a month now, Mars has been easy to see as it rises earlier and gets high into the sky."}, {"id": "6", "subevent": "Opposition occurs approximately every 26 months."}, {"id": "7", "subevent": "Nasa describes the phenomenon, explaining that during opposition, Mars rises in the east as the sun sets in the west, stays up all night, and sets in the west as the sun rises in the east."}, {"id": "8", "subevent": "Nasa notes that if Earth and Mars followed perfectly circular orbits, opposition would be as close as the two planets could get."}, {"id": "9", "subevent": "Despite cloudy weather forecast for parts of the UK, Mars should be visible among breaks and even through lighter cloud, Ms Banyard added."}, {"id": "10", "subevent": "Ms Banyard said Mars should be visible with the naked eye, but recommended using a four-inch telescope with 24-millimetre magnification."}, {"id": "11", "subevent": "With the naked eye, Mars will look like a blurry orange star, but with a telescope, stargazers should be able to make out surface features."}, {"id": "12", "subevent": "The next time Mars will be this big and bright will be in 2033."}]}
